day: # Rows keyed to a Sunday that land between 24 December and 5 January are left to the dated rows.
# RCL Daily Readings (Consultation on Common Texts, 2005), as given by the
# (Years A, B and C as dated for 2025-26, 2026-27 and 2027-28, read October 2026).
# The readings of Thursday to Saturday prepare for the coming Sunday and those of
# Monday to Wednesday reflect on the past one, so each weekday is keyed to its
# Sunday (the same date rules as rcl.csv) with an offset; its `when` bounds are
# moved by the same offset, so that a weekday is kept only when its Sunday is.
# The days from 24 December to 5 January are given by date.  Weeks that did not
# occur in those three years (after the 6th to 9th Sundays after the Epiphany
# Proper 3 and some of Proper 4) are missing.  After Pentecost both series are given
# (semicontinuous: psalm_s, ot_s; complementary: psalm_c, ot_c).  Obvious slips in
# the source text (book names run together, "Chronicales") were corrected.
# Filled from liturgical-calendar.com, "Revised Common Lectionary Daily Readings"
# (https://liturgical-calendar.com/en/DailyRCL/), for the weeks the three Vanderbilt years lack:
# after the 5th to 8th Sundays after the Epiphany, Propers 3 to 5, the Advent 4 week
# and the dated days 22-23 December and 7-9 January (the first to third days after the
# Epiphany, kept unless the Thursday before the Baptism has come).  The two sources were
# compared on days they share and agree.
# Checked against the ELCA's yearly lists (Year C 2024-25, Year A 2025-26), which
# corrected the Monday to Wednesday of Easter Week in Years A and C (a day late
# before), four readings (Year C: Ezekiel 1:1-2:1, 2 Kings 18:19-25; 19:1-7,
# 2 Kings 15:1-7, Proverbs 15:8-11, 24-33; confirmed by Bible Gateway's plan) and
# gave 26 December and 2 January of Year C (its 2 January Old Testament, printed
# "Proverbs 147:12-20", is taken as Year B's Proverbs 1:1-7, with the same James).
# A few dated days of Years A and B are still missing.
